advisory.finding: New decision text was inserted into accepted ADR 0005 D2 (docs/adr/0005-snapshot-cache-architecture.md:77-87) as plain body text, with no amendment or erratum label. It sets a new architectural rule: populate, evict, drain, and sweep all share one store-wide accounting lock, and a donor build holds that lock from its candidate search through publish. The ADR is still 'Status: Accepted, Date: 2026-06-26', so a reader cannot tell this rule was added after acceptance. D5 also still says 'population stays lock-free' (line 139), with no note that donor-build populations now hold a store-wide flock that evictions wait on.
scenarios: A maintainer reads D2 and cannot tell the accounting-lock rule came after the accepted decision of 2026-06-26, or which bug led to it, without searching history.
A reader of D5 sees 'population stays lock-free' and finds no note that donor builds now hold a store-wide flock that evictions wait on.

The existing test at tests/unit/test_snapshot_janitor.py:724-726 already has this kind of check: `assert sum(cache.entry_size(e) for e in entries) > on_disk`, commented as making the assertion 'discriminating, not satisfied by every possible accounting'.
advisory.finding: test_a_populate_links_from_an_entry_before_that_entry_measures (and, the same way, test_evict_measures_then_a_populate_links_from_the_victim) only checks byte_total == _real_store_bytes. It never checks that the second populate actually built by hardlinking from the paused entry. If no hardlinks are created, the totals match no matter how the actors interleave. So if _adjacent_shas stopped producing donor-eligible commits, or _donor_candidates/_diff_paths stopped picking the neighbour, the test would stay green on a tree that has the ordering bug. Test 2 has a built-in check (it fails if _link_tree_paths is never called); tests 1 and 3 have none.
scenarios: A later change to donor selection or to the size threshold at delta_tree.py:256 makes adjacent SHAs build in full. Tests 1 and 3 keep passing even if the accounting_lock ordering is removed.

src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:497-500: the outer `except BaseException: shutil.rmtree(build, ...)` in materialize also removes the build, but only after the accounting lock has been released. A test that only checks that the build is gone in the end cannot tell the two apart.
advisory.finding: No test covers the new failure branch of _build_publish_account. When the donor attempt raises after creating hardlinks, the `discard` directories must be removed while the accounting lock is still held, so a later eviction does not read inflated link counts. A concrete input that would show a regression: make `_apply_delta` (called after `_link_tree_paths` succeeded) raise OSError during `cache.acquire(b)`, then call `janitor._evict` on donor a and compare byte_total with _real_store_bytes. If the in-lock discard were dropped, only the outer handler in materialize would remove the links. It runs after the lock is released, which is exactly the window the commit says it closes.
scenarios: A refactor removes the in-lock discard because the outer handler 'already cleans up'. An evictor running between the lock release and the outer rmtree sees a donor file at two links, credits nothing for it, and the total drifts. No test fails.

dropped.finding: The store-wide accounting lock is held through the donor candidate search (up to 17 git subprocesses, each with a 300 s timeout) and not just around the hardlink, delta, publish and increment steps. As a result, all concurrent cache-miss populates (and evictions) across threads and processes run one at a time.
scenarios: N concurrent requests for distinct new ticket tips (the stated reason for the donor path: 'Fast-moving ticket tips rarely hit cache') each wait for the previous N-1 donor searches; latency grows as O(N × donor-build time)
A slow or hung ls-tree/diff in one process holds the lock for up to 300 s per call and blocks every other populate, every janitor eviction, and every add_bytes caller across all processes
The janitor GC pass's evictions queue behind long donor holds, which delays free-space reclamation while the store is under disk pressure
dropped.suggested_fix: Split materialize_via_donor into a lock-free planning phase (target ls-tree, candidate listing, per-candidate ls-tree and diff, producing a list of (donor_entry, link_paths, deletes, writes) plans) and a linking phase. Run only the linking phase (_link_tree_paths, _apply_delta, publish, exclusive_size, add_bytes_held) inside accounting_lock. If a planned donor was evicted in between, os.link fails and the existing fall-through to the next candidate or a full build preserves correctness.
